preconditions.description: The number of BubbleCores N is an integer between 3 and 15,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= U != V < N for U, V in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge (U, V) connects two distinct BubbleCores with indices in [0, N-1].
There are exactly N edges, forming a tree (no cycles, all nodes connected).

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(line, str) for line in stdin.splitlines())
preconditions.description: Input is a sequence of lines where the first line is N and the next N lines are edge pairs.

postconditions.description: The output is a single integer representing the maximum possible sum of all BubbleCores' potentials, where `max_sum_potentials` is defined as the optimal sum achievable by choosing a kick-start node and a valid activation order.

postconditions.expression: max_sum_potentials(N, edges) == sum(potential(core, activation_order) for core in range(N)) for some valid activation_order starting with the kick-start node
postconditions.description: The sum is computed by evaluating the potential of each BubbleCore at the moment it is activated, where `potential(core, order)` is the number of inactive BubbleCores in the connected component of `core` at the time of activation (including itself).

The potential of a BubbleCore at activation is the size of its connected component of inactive BubbleCores (including itself) at that moment, where `inactive_component(core, order)` is the set of all inactive BubbleCores reachable from `core` via inactive BubbleCores at the time of activation.
